thread:
Alex M: Quick question — where should compression live in the telemetry flow? SDK/edge, collector/ingest, or a hybrid? Thinking about trace/metric/log envelopes and how it affects sampling & cost attribution.

Priya S: TL;DR: edge compress saves network $ for customers but ruins any in-flight attribute inspection unless we put indexable metadata outside the compressed blob. Edge CPU variability is a concern too.

Marco: If we accept SDK-level gzip, collectors will need to decompress to do attribute-based sampling/routing. That creates CPU spikes and memory pressure on collectors.

Li Chen: Also a reliability point: compressed monolithic batches make partial recovery hard if a connection drops. Uncompressed chunking allows partial ingestion and stitch.

Alex M: Right. We could keep a small plaintext header with routing/billing fields and compress only the body. That lets the ingest plane tag & route cheaply.

Priya S: I'd frame the design around two decisions: (A) where to compress, (B) the compression unit: per-record vs per-batch vs per-tenant bundle. Each affects latency/cost/enrich semantics.

Marco: Proposed options + tradeoffs: 
- Option A: No SDK compression; collectors accept raw -> simpler routing, more network cost to customers.
- Option B: SDK compression with Content-Encoding header -> enables network savings but collector must decompress to inspect body.
- Option C: hdr/body split: hdr plaintext + body compressed -> best of both worlds for routing but requires SDK change and envelope spec tweak.

Li Chen: For cost attribution we need stable, indexable keys (tenant_id, billing_key) in the outer header. If sampling selectors sometimes live in body, we need a small set of common selectors duplicated to hdr as an index. Backcompat via schema_version.

Marco: Implementation detail: hdr/body split example: 
```
{ "hdr": { "tenant": "acme-inc", "billing_key": "bk_prod_01", "schema_v": "3" },
  "body_encoding": "gzip",
  "body": "<base64 gzip>"
}
```
Collector can route/cost-tag on hdr without decompressing. Decompression invoked lazily when enrichment or sampling requires it.

Alex M: Edge case: field-level sampling where sampled field only exists in body. We must require SDKs to populate a tiny sampling-index in hdr for selectors we care about. Otherwise sampling accuracy suffers.

Priya S: Agree. This implies a contract: SDKs must fill reserved hdr fields for sampling and billing at schema_v >= 3. We should publish migration guidance.

infra-bot: Note: collector v2.4.0 in staging accepts Content-Encoding + exposes decompress_success/decompress_failure metrics.

Li Chen: Perf telemetry we need: decompress ops/sec, avg CPU/ms per decompress, envelope_size histo, and failed_decompress_count. Also track bytes saved by compression per-tenant.

Marco: Danger: large compressed bundles (50MB) force whole-buffer buffering on collector. Add max_envelope_size and require chunked multipart uploads beyond threshold. Chunking semantics must allow reassembly in case of partial failures.

Alex M: Proposed next steps: 
- Draft short RFC for hdr/body compression contract with examples + compatibility matrix (Priya + Li)
- Perf microbench for gzip/brotli/zstd on our collector instances (Marco)
- SDK guidance: default no-compress for small events, auto-compress > 1MB, always keep hdr plaintext (Alex)
- Collector metrics & limits: implement decompress metrics and max_envelope_size enforcement (infra team)

Priya S: I'll author the RFC. Will include appendix on sampling-index fields and fallback behaviour when body is unavailable.

Marco: I'll run perf tests and upload results here in 5 business days.

Li Chen: I'll spec chunking + failure semantics and a small state machine for reassembly; include how we mark events as "body-unavailable" while retaining hdr for billing.

Alex M: If there are no objections, we'll adopt hdr/body split as recommended pattern and keep SDK compression opt-in for now so we can measure. Volunteers to review RFC?

Priya S: I'll review.

Marco: +1

infra-bot: Reminder: staging collector rollout scheduled 2026-05-03 02:00 UTC.

Alex M: Great — thanks all. We'll loop back after RFC and perf numbers.
